A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same VISTA study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-ranking analyses, benchmark evaluations of VISTA, efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 3 and Appendices A-C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including CHAIR, POPE, MME, and MMHal-Bench evaluations, token-ranking analyses, ablations, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Sections 2.3-2.4 retain the same per-image visual steering vector, normalized residual-stream intervention, and self-logits augmentation through early-layer averaging and weighted combination. No algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MSCOCO captioning and token-analysis data, POPE COCO subset, MMHal-Bench, and MME evaluations. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The vanilla, DoLa, VCD, OPERA, and PAI comparisons retain their membership within corresponding experiments. VTI is added only to related work, without evaluation. PAI's citation changes from 2024f to 2024g, but the comparator itself is unchanged.

E3.justification: The architectures, decoding strategies, samples, prompts, metrics, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. For example, CHAIR still uses 500 MSCOCO validation images and a 512-token generation limit; beam size remains 5 and nucleus sampling uses top-p = 0.9.

E4.justification: The token-ranking analyses, VSV/SLA parameter ablations, window-size analysis, efficiency comparison, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged, including the supplementary analyses in Appendices A-C.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same averages and point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains greedy LLaVA-1.5 VISTA CHAIR-S/CHAIR-I scores of 20.4/6.9, and Table 5 retains its latency of 36.32 ms/token.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8, token-category and ranking definitions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the same three token-dynamics observations, two-module training-free VISTA contribution, and approximately 40% hallucination-reduction claim. The claimed experimental scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including architecture-dependent tuning, visual-encoder dependence, single-round applicability, oracle bias, and embedding-space mismatch. The final limitations lines move onto page 9 in v2; they are already present in v1.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A retain the same hyperparameters, prompts, token-processing rules, aggregation instructions, and algorithm documentation. The VISTA code link is unchanged; surrounding punctuation edits do not alter access information.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds VTI and its reference, acknowledging a related representation-engineering approach while distinguishing its focus on unstable visual representations. The summary of prior methods' supervision and decoding constraints changes from 'and' to 'or'. PAI's citation suffix is consequently relabeled.

P1.justification: Limited wording corrections include adding 'and' to the image-description sentence and replacing 'set aside VISTA with' with 'compare VISTA with'. v2 also updates affiliation and proceedings text and adds the brief VTI discussion. Section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: No figures or tables are added, removed, or redesigned. The updated first-page publication footer and added related-work/reference text cause limited layout reflow, including continuation of the limitations paragraph onto page 9.

improvement.justification: The added VTI discussion fills a limited gap in related-work coverage and clarifies the relationship to another latent-steering approach. Small wording corrections also improve clarity. Methods, empirical support, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is modest.
